text:
Russia and Ukraine said Thursday that demining operations around the Russia n-held town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine were finished and that evacuations and aid deliveries in the area could begin.
Efforts have been underway for several weeks to organize a relief operation for the town's residents, who have faced acute shortages of food and medicine. Russia seized Oleshky shortly after President Vladimir Putin ordered the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Both sides of the conflict have praised U.S. first lady Melania Trump for helping broker the ceasefire, which is limited to the area around Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson.
"Demining operations of routes have been completed for the humanitarian mission in Oleshky," Ukraine and Russia said in virtually identical statements. "The humanitarian convoy is ready for departure."
The convoy will head to a local hospital, and residents wishing to leave will be allowed to do so within a specific time frame. Aid packages will then be delivered, the statements read.
Ukraine's human rights chief, Dmytro Lubinets, referred to Melania Trump when he extended Kyiv's "special thanks" to someone who was "personally devoting her time and attention to the humanitarian mission and assistance to civilians in Oleshky."
Still, any hope of wider relief in the war appears to have been dashed away by a series of attacks on Ukrainian cities in recent days, including a strike on the main train station in the southeastern city of Dnipro that killed at least 14 people on Thursday.
Neither Russia nor Ukraine has reported any violations of the ceasefire in Oleshky since it began on Tuesday. The pause in fighting is expected to last until Sunday.
